records.title: Prologue
records.summary: The game's tutorial chapter in and around Laslea village, played entirely in daylight on a hard budget of eight time segments.
bodyParagraphs: Coen's story opens in Laslea Glen before the wider valley unlocks. Almost every job on offer here is flagged as time-sensitive, and the chapter ends when the day does, so the eight daytime segments you start with are the whole budget.

Guides agree you cannot clear the board: Dexerto's quest hub puts the cost of doing every prologue task at roughly seventeen segments against the eight you are given, which forces a triage pass on your very first hour of play.

Prologue side quests are the only permanently missable content in the game. Once the chapter closes they vanish for good, while everything in the open world after it stays available right up to the final assault.
records.note: The eight-segment figure is the daylight budget the prologue gives you rather than a per-quest charge; the seventeen-segment figure is what sources say clearing every prologue task would demand.

bodyParagraphs: Deep Down is one of the timed prologue tasks that disappears when the chapter ends. Prologue routing guides list it among the jobs worth spending segments on, specifically because pulling Lazar out alive is treated as the good outcome.
Sources place it in Laslea Glen, though Fextralife's regional index also files a Deep Down entry under Maragir Wealds.
records.note: Region is contested: prologue guides treat this as a Laslea Glen job, while Fextralife's Maragir Wealds page also lists a quest of this name.

records.title: A Friend Like This
records.summary: The opening beat of Lacra's questline, picked up in a back alley in the north-east of Svartrau City.
bodyParagraphs: A Friend Like This starts in an alley under the walls in the north-eastern corner of Svartrau City. Guides quote 150 XP for finishing it, and completing it is what puts Song of the Mountain on the board.
It is the first link in the six-quest Lacra chain that eventually leads to Midnight Reckoning and The Patricide ending, so it is effectively the gate on one of the game's seven endings.

records.title: Fall Before Dusk
records.summary: The closing quest of Crake's chain and the route to The Knyazmaker ending.
bodyParagraphs: Fall Before Dusk resolves the Manumit route. The Knyazmaker requires siding with Crake and the Manumits and putting Catalin Dragosti back in power.
The critical moment comes when Brencis attacks Catalin in the throne room: intervening is what keeps both Catalin and Crake alive, and beating Brencis from there is what unlocks the ending.
Guides call this the longest of the ally endings precisely because of how much Manumit work has to be banked before Rise at Dawn even starts.

records.title: Echoes of Silenced Bells
records.summary: Anca's opening quest, a monastery investigation that costs roughly a full phase of time.
bodyParagraphs: Echoes of Silenced Bells is one of the first things the open world offers, and it takes Coen into St. Tyna's monastery with Anca. Completing the prologue quest Smoke and Ashes is the stated prerequisite.

It is expensive. Guides put the total at eight time segments for 150 XP, with one source quoting nine depending on choices. The published breakdown charges a segment each for pushing through the fog, escorting Anca toward the convent, investigating the chapel, telling Anca it is time for the library, and moving the candle along the spine to reveal the writing that ends the quest.
Spending two segments at the close rolls you straight into Between the Words and moves the party to the inn.

Start point is contested. Different guides put it at the Laslea Glen village gates, at one of the broken shrines in the Briar Sloughs, and at St. Tyna's Grove itself. The monastery it revolves around is in St. Tyna's Grove, which is why the region is recorded that way here.
records.note: Total cost is given as 8 segments by most guides and 9 by at least one, depending on choices. The starting location is reported three different ways (Laslea Glen village gates, a broken shrine in the Briar Sloughs, and St. Tyna's Grove).

records.title: Most Precious Thing
records.summary: A short quest nested inside Echoes of Silenced Bells, about St. Tyna's stolen necklace.
bodyParagraphs: Most Precious Thing opens while Coen is travelling with Anca on Echoes of Silenced Bells and wraps up as she heads for the library. Brencis's men want St. Tyna's necklace and will trade safe passage for it.

The route runs through the chapel, St. Tyna's coffin, the keys in the shed beside the sacristy, and a body on the sacristy floor holding the relic. Handing it over forces a choice between securing the soldiers' passage and abandoning them.
Completion pays 150 XP. Guides charge one time segment for the chapel investigation step, but no source found gives a total for the quest, so no cost is recorded.

records.title: Between the Words
records.summary: Anca's second quest, a night of forbidden books at Tyna's Monastery that pays unusually well.
bodyParagraphs: Between the Words follows on automatically from Echoes of Silenced Bells, with Anca giving it at Tyna's Monastery. The reward is 1000 XP and a skill point, which is generous for the length.

The published costs disagree: one walkthrough puts the total at four segments, two of them spent studying the forbidden books, while another says two. The individual actions described are brewing Anca a warm drink for a segment and interacting with the books for another.
Both figures are recorded as a range rather than picking a winner.

records.title: Where Old Devils Lie
records.summary: Anca's third quest, a trek from the Crossroads Inn to ruins hiding the Font of Life.
bodyParagraphs: Where Old Devils Lie starts at the Crossroads Inn, south-east of St. Tyna's Grove, with Anca as quest giver. Guides put it at 150 XP across four total time segments.

There is a hard wait attached: after Between the Words you have to let a full in-game day pass, sixteen segments, before Anca will continue. Returning to her and choosing to go looking for the Font of Life begins the quest proper.

From there the route runs north through wolves, uphill to a vantage point that triggers a cutscene, then north-east along the river to ruins whose entrance sits behind a statue. Several conversations along the way feed Anca's romance.

records.title: Stronger Than Achilles
records.summary: Anca's final quest, a run of trials beneath the ruins that ends at the Font of Life.
bodyParagraphs: Stronger Than Achilles begins the instant Where Old Devils Lie ends, at the mouth of the ancient ruins, with the single objective of completing the trials and getting back out.

Progress runs through undead in the depths, a blood sacrifice to open the way, a Fallen Hero boss, and a central grate that spawns Guardians of the Font before opening access to the idol at the heart of the room.

There is only enough left in the Font for one person and the decision is final. Coen drinking unlocks the Font of Life witchcraft perk, Anca drinking strips away her witchcraft, and destroying the Font reveals the legendary Ancient Greaves.
Rewards are 500 XP, a skill point and the Sins of the Past trophy, plus whichever of the Font outcomes you picked. No segment cost is published.

records.title: A Study in Crimson
records.summary: The opening of Vicho's questline: a night-time murder investigation across Svartrau's rooftops.
bodyParagraphs: Vicho keeps his emporium in the northern part of Svartrau City, west of the Market Tower. He is Vrakhiri and cannot be out in daylight, so this one is night-only. Getting in means using Shadowstep to climb the neighbouring houses and jumping to his balcony.
From there Vicho takes to the rooftops and leads Coen to the jeweller's house, where the victims are: Devora's corpse and a note upstairs, Eli's body in the basement.
Rewards total 750 XP across the objectives, plus a skill point and the Mercenary's Amulet, and Vicho opens up as a witchcraft vendor.
The quest reads as finished after the meeting, but the thread continues: the next daytime period puts The Good Samaritan on a medic in Svartrau.

records.title: The Good Samaritan
records.summary: Vicho's second chapter: a daytime medicine delivery south of Svartrau that turns into a crime scene.
bodyParagraphs: The Good Samaritan appears on the medic in the centre of Svartrau during the first daytime period after A Study in Crimson. The job is to run medicaments out to a farm south of the city.

The route: travel to the farm in The Silts, use Focus Mode and Compel Soul on the dead woman in the cabin with the Farmer's Sword and Wedding Headband as catalysts, follow the tracks into the wheat field, kill the wolves, read the note on the daughter's body, and return to the medic in daylight.
It matters beyond its own rewards. Finishing it is what unlocks the Unquenchable Thirst confrontation, the moment that decides whether Vicho lives.
Published costs disagree: one guide says a single time segment, another says three.
records.note: Time cost is given as 1 segment by one guide and 3 by another.

records.summary: The confrontation that closes Vicho's questline and decides whether he survives.
bodyParagraphs: Unquenchable Thirst is described as the confrontation with Vicho unlocked by completing The Good Samaritan, and it is the point where his fate is settled. Guides on keeping Vicho alive centre on the dialogue choices and blood deliveries leading into it.
Sources describe it as the culmination of the Vicho thread rather than labelling it a standalone quest entry, so its classification here is provisional.

records.title: Good Home
records.summary: The gateway quest to the Sanzhani chain, and the widest published cost range of any quest found.
bodyParagraphs: Good Home starts north of Svartrau City near the Sandy Gorge Shrine, where a stone ringed by red mushrooms triggers it. Following the glowing mushroom rings through the forest leads to a burrow and a girl named Heile, who wants her brother found.
The brother is Tonis, at the burner camp. Loosening him up with a drink is the cheap way through; he can then be walked back to the Yawning Burrow.

The cost swings hard on how you play it. Guides quote two to eight segments: the cheapest run skips the optional investigations and uses the drink, the most expensive inspects every clue and offers to swing an axe.
It is the prerequisite for the rest of the Sanzhani questline, which is the only source of extra days in the game.

records.title: Letters to Lunka
records.summary: The Sanzhani payoff quest, and the only quest found that gives time back instead of taking it.
bodyParagraphs: Letters to Lunka closes the Sanzhani chain. The approach involves following glowing moths from flowerbed to flowerbed in the Svartrau Outskirts until a small opening appears.
Once the rest of the Sanzhani quests are done and the Sanzhana Tsarina has been asked about all the letters, you wait one in-game day for the reply.

The reward is the reason everyone points at this quest: a full extra in-game day, sixteen time segments, plus 250 XP for reading all five of Lunka's replies. Against a thirty-day deadline that is a meaningful extension.
Sources phrase the requirement slightly differently, some saying the other four Sanzhani quests in any order, others saying all five, which is really the same chain counted with or without Good Home.
records.note: Sources describe the requirement as either 'the remaining four Sanzhani quests' or 'all five Sanzhani quests', a counting difference over whether Good Home is included.

records.title: Buried Past
records.summary: Volk's multi-day chore chain, widely called the single most expensive side quest in the game.
bodyParagraphs: Volk lives in a hut north-east of Svartrau City near the Ruined Hut Shrine; the merchant at the Maragir Crossroads can mark the spot on your map.

The structure is what makes it costly. Every visit to Volk ends with having to wait until the next day before the thread moves, required interactions charge a segment per day, and the optional chores add more on top. Locating Pieter's treasure alone is quoted at four segments.
Doing all of Volk's optional chores is the stated condition for the best outcome and for stopping him betraying you.
Rewards are substantial: legendary armour, a powerful sword ability, and a chunk of backstory about Coen's father.

Published figures range from nine to twelve segments, to sixteen once the full-day waits are counted, to twenty in both the day and night versions, which one guide frames as more than four per cent of the entire thirty-day clock spent on one side quest.
records.note: Time cost is heavily contested: 9-12, 16, and 20 segments are all published figures. Region is also unclear, described as north-east of Svartrau City but reached via Maragir Crossroads, so no region slug is recorded.

records.title: Of Wolves and Men
records.summary: A side quest most guides say is entirely free of time cost, though one source disagrees sharply.
bodyParagraphs: The majority of current guides state that Of Wolves and Men takes zero segments off the thirty-day clock: picking it up does not push the day forward and it does not eat into the family deadline, which makes it an easy yes.
One time-cost catalogue instead lists it at ten units. That figure is recorded here as the upper bound rather than discarded, but the weight of sources is on zero.
Timing still matters for a different reason. The payoff depends on Compel Soul, a witchcraft ability Coen can only use in human form during daylight, so the quest wants to be run in the day.
records.note: Flatly contested: most guides say 0 time segments, one time-cost catalogue says 10.

records.title: The Beast of Balaur
records.summary: A hellhound hunt in the mountains west of Parlita, priced at three time segments for 250 XP.
bodyParagraphs: The quest triggers on entering the area around the Mount Balaur Shrine, on the western edge of the forest in the mountains west of Parlita. Focus Mode picks up tracks that climb the left-hand path.

The trail ends at a cave full of skeletons; inspecting them and crouching through the gap at the back reveals the miniboss, a vicious hellhound called the Beast of Balaur. Killing it and looting the nearby body yields A Letter to Iancu.
The wrap-up is with Ciprian, in the northern house next to the Parlita Shrine, and it is that conversation the sources price at three time segments. Total reward is 250 XP.
Boar's Back sits inside Bakir's fiefdom alongside Rockfalls, which is why the court is recorded as Bakir here.
records.note: Court assignment comes from Fextralife's statement that Bakir's fiefdom covers Boar's Back and Rockfalls, not from the quest page itself.

records.title: Night Terrors
records.summary: An unmarked night-only quest down a well behind Svartrau cathedral, priced at a single segment.
bodyParagraphs: Night Terrors never appears on the map. It starts when Coen walks into the courtyard north of the Svartrau City cathedral at night and hears noise coming from underground.
Focus Mode traces the howling to the well. Popping the top and dropping in leads along a passage, through a gap on the left, to a body in the next chamber; inspecting it ends the quest.
It costs one time segment and pays 75 XP, which makes it one of the cheapest quests with a published price.
Triggering Night Terrors at all appears to lock out A Dubious Gift, the quest attached to the Xanthe court activity Cathedral Ritual. Finding the note also rolls straight into A Monk and a Saint.

records.title: A Pilgrimage for Power
records.summary: A four-part hunt for hidden Uriashi Sacred Stones that never places a marker on your map.
bodyParagraphs: A Pilgrimage for Power is the one quest chain in the game that gives you no map marker at all. Each of the four Uriashi Sacred Stones is found by travelling to the right region and walking uphill toward the sound of wind chimes.
The four legs are Bear Trouble, Dark-Thing, The Ritual and Fanatics, and the stones sit in the Briar Sloughs, Rockfalls, the Tantari Woods and St. Tyna's Grove.
Each stone is guarded by something different: a Ravenous Bear, an Essence of Grief, wolves among fanatic corpses, and a Witch boss.

Inspecting each Uriashi Glyph costs two time segments and pays a Ravenous Flock Manual plus 250 XP. Completing all four unlocks the Ravenous Flock witchcraft ability at full strength, which guides rate among the strongest combat options in the tree.
Recorded here as a contract-style repeatable chain because it is a templated hunt rather than a character storyline.
records.note: Classified as 'contract' for its repeatable templated structure; the game's own category label for this chain was not confirmed in the sources found.

records.title: Destroyed Shrines
records.summary: A repeatable questline covering seventeen wrecked shrines, each one restored by recovering its stolen heart.
bodyParagraphs: There are seventeen destroyed shrines in the valley, and each follows the same shape: inspect the damaged shrine to start its quest, hold Focus Mode to reveal the thief's footprints, follow them to a camp, a corpse or an animal, loot the heart, then return and restore the shrine.
Restoring a shrine turns it back into a working fast-travel point, which is why guides treat this as high-value busywork rather than filler.

ul: Small Bridge, south of Stoneward Post
Western Slopes, west along the road from Stelian's Redoubt
Bear's Maw, east of Mert's Mill
Crossroads Inn, just west of the inn and east of St. Tyna's Convent

bodyParagraphs: No complete list of all seventeen surfaced in the sources found.
